results.reader_title: Supply security policy should address underdiversification without decoupling
results.reader_what: Public intervention can be warranted when firms underinvest in diversified supply sources because systemic disruption costs exceed their private incentives.
results.reader_why: Resilience requires managing technical, environmental, geopolitical and market shocks without unnecessarily costly blanket decoupling.
results.reader_more: The authors distinguish market failures, public intervention and private incentives in supplier diversification; they recommend data on essential inputs and EU trade partnerships while warning against self-sufficiency for its own sake.

deep_analysis.research_question: When should EU policy intervene to correct security-of-supply market failures?
deep_analysis.main_finding: Felbermayr and Janeba show why market incentives may yield insufficient diversification of strategic suppliers and argue for targeted EU policies to strengthen supply security without blanket decoupling.
deep_analysis.method_or_basis: Original full scholarly article and EconStor archived complete PDF; industrial economics with policy guidelines.
deep_analysis.qualification: Normative economic analysis with economic-theory mechanisms and examples; the policy levers are proposals rather than demonstrated outcomes.
deep_analysis.radar_relevance: Core methodological EU supply-security and strategic dependence study.
